gist: Atwood gathers adepts' testimony that the root, seed and Mercury of the Hermetic work lie in man (his vital fire, blood and spirit), then restates this through three principles of attraction, repulsion and circulation: human life is out of balance, and the Art uses an Antimonial Spirit / Invisible Mercury to harmonize them, beginning with a blackening called the head of Hermes' crow.

notes.point: The preceding adept's assertions help explain Trismegistus: the work is in us and about us; the mystery lies in hidden elements.
Geber: who knows no natural principles in himself lacks the true root for the labor.
Basil: metals have one root; mercury, salt, sulfur (spirit, body, soul) lie together in one well-known thing, a golden seed or magnet, without destroying metals; it is real.
Crollius: the light and mineral vapor producing gold in the earth is also in man, generating all creatures.
Albertus Magnus: gold is everywhere, but the highest mineral virtue is in man, where fire, the aurific principle, burns brightest.
Our Mercury is fiery, vital, prepared and coagulated in the innermost chamber of life.
Verse: man, noblest creature, is the mine from which a costless natural mercury is brought by art.
Philosophers said little (the work being short, per Maria) but found and increased the hidden elements.
Aliphili: man, by the water and earth in himself, unknowingly produces the true fiery water, which reduces even gold to black earth yielding water and mild salt; poor and rich have it equally.

Hermes: the aspirant must quit vice and be just and helpful; the vicious defile by evil imagination the Spirit to be refined. Crollius' true physician is sincere and knows all qualities lie in salt, mercury, sulfur.
These three principles, attraction, repulsion, circulation, are in all.
Verse: blood holds the three things and gold's nature, is the principal matter of growth, found without cost in the noblest.
Morien: the thing is extracted from the king himself and increases by love and delight.

Modern adepts call man's life an unmingled fire capable of melioration. The diffused Matter could partly be taken anywhere, but the aim is to perfect it and manifest the Causal light. How the human circulatory system can be made to comprehend all inferior existences and supersede nature may be gathered from this philosophy, which gives reasons for choosing the most noble subject and only vessel.

Attraction (occult), repulsion (its reaction) and circulation (their conflict) move everything, including chemical affinity. Predominance gives ellipse, equilibrium a circle; circulation harmonizes if the matter is qualified.
Nature lost balance; human life drifts to dissolution; only the Antimonial Spirit rectified by Art, balanced in attraction and repulsion, withstands this.
Bohme: the Invisible Mercury, spiritual air of Antimony, prepares this spirit by harmonizing the three principles.
This is the vital spirit of arterial blood, where repulsion predominates, drawing consciousness from its First Cause; the Art occults the opposing principle to restore the true rector.
Latin: salt of blood transmuted by urinous ferment; Solve, Coagula, Fige.
Hermes: one must know to mortify, generate, vivify, cleanse and illuminate until whiteness rises from blackness.

Modern exponent: after three months' circulation the powder blackens; the attraction of the fixed and repulsion of the volatile are slain by circulation and all rest: the head of Hermes' crow. The fixed sentient medium dissolves, revealing original evil and the principle of rectification.

method.veiled: the work is both in us and about us
method.plain: The subject of the work lies within the human being, not only in outer nature.
method.basis: II.1 ¶11 literal wording; reinforced by ¶12 (gold-producing vapor 'is also in man'), ¶16 ('extracted from thee'), ¶17 ('the most noble subject').

also.text: the whole mystery is comprehended in the hidden elements of his Wisdom

method.veiled: he who in himself knows no natural principles, is very remote from this sacred science, because he has not the true root in him
method.plain: The operator must know the natural principles within himself; the root of the work is in him.

method.veiled: there is a nearer place yet in which these three, viz., the mercury, slat and sulfur --- spirit, body and soul --- lie hid together in one thing, well known
method.plain: Mercury, salt and sulfur, glossed as spirit, body and soul, are found together in one well-known thing, so metals need not be broken down to get them.
method.basis: II.1 ¶11 gives the gloss and the contrast with destroying metals.

also.text: this golden seed or magnet
this metallic seed, or root

method.veiled: the same light and mineral vapor, which produces gold within the bowels of the earth is also in man
method.plain: The generative agent that forms gold in the earth is present in man and generates all creatures.
method.basis: II.1 ¶12: 'the same is the generating spirit of all creatures'.

method.veiled: fire, which is the true aurific principle in the life of all, burns more than all glorious in him erect
method.plain: The gold-making principle is fire in the life of all things, strongest in man; hence the highest mineral virtue is in man.
method.basis: II.1 ¶12: 'the highest mineral virtue nevertheless resides in man; for fire...'.

method.veiled: Our Mercury is philosophic, fiery, vital
method.plain: The philosophic Mercury is a living fire, prepared and coagulated within the innermost seat of life.
method.basis: II.1 ¶12: 'prepared in the innermost chamber of life, and there it is coagulated'; read with the fire in man just before.

also.text: it is prepared in the innermost chamber of life, and there it is coagulated

method.veiled: A naturall mercuryalyte which cost right nought, Out of hy myner by arte yt most be brought
method.plain: Man (the noblest creature, with the four elements proportioned) is the mine; a free natural mercury must be drawn out of him by art.
method.basis: II.1 ¶12-13: 'hy myner' follows 'man, ys most noble creature ... In whom are the fowre elements'.

also.text: For our mettalls be nought ells but miners too, Of our Soon and Moone

method.veiled: producest an essence, called, by us, the expert, the great and miraculous mystery of the world; that is the true fiery water
method.plain: Man, by conjoining the elements of water and earth within himself, produces the essence called the true fiery water, without knowing it.
method.basis: II.1 ¶14 names the essence and its source in man.

also.text: through the breath and power of the water and earth in thyself, conjoinest the elements and makest them one

method.veiled: it dissolves radically, incrudates even the mature, constant, and very fixed, fiery and abiding mass and matter of gold, and reduces it into a fit black earth, like to black spittle
method.plain: The fiery water is a universal solvent that returns even fixed gold to a raw state, a black earth from which a water and a mild salt are obtained.

also.text: wherein we find a water and the true salt destitute of all odor, vehemency, and corrosive nature of the fire

method.veiled: the poor as well as the rich may have it in the same equal plenty
method.plain: The matter is free and equally available to everyone.
method.basis: II.1 ¶14; ¶13 'cost right nought'; ¶15 'without labour or cost'.

also.text: The true blood to find without labour or cost
which cost right nought

method.veiled: to quit himself from the usurpations of vice, to be good and just and of a profound reason, ready at hand to help mankind
method.plain: The operator must be morally purified, just, reasoning deeply and benevolent.

also.text: true, sincere, intelligent, faithful

method.veiled: being destitute of light, defile by an evil imagination the very Spirit that ought to be refined
method.plain: The idle or vicious operator corrupts, through his imagination, the Spirit that is the material refined in the work.
method.basis: II.1 ¶14: the defiling is by 'evil imagination', and the Spirit is what 'ought to be refined', implying the operator's mind acts on the matter.

method.veiled: these three principles of attraction, repulsion, and circulation, the universal accord of life, are everywhere and in all
method.plain: Salt, mercury and sulfur are restated as attraction, repulsion and circulation, present in everything.
method.basis: II.1 ¶14: 'these three principles' directly follows 'salt, mercury, and sulfur'; see ambiguities.

method.veiled: For blood is the principle matter of each thing, Which hath any manner of increasing
method.plain: Blood contains the three principles and the nature of gold and is the principal matter of growth; it is to be sought in 'the noblest'.
method.basis: II.1 ¶15 states blood's role; 'the noblest' read against ¶12 'man, ys most noble creature' and ¶17 'the most noble subject'.

also.text: Blood containeth the three things I have told, And in his tincture hath nature of gold
See out the noblest, as I said before

method.veiled: The thing, O king, is extracted from thee, in the which mineral thou dost even exist
method.plain: The matter of the Stone is drawn from the person himself; it grows when tested 'by the love and delight in thee'.

also.text: when thou shalt have proved all by the love and delight in thee, it will increase

method.veiled: a pure, naked, and unmingled fire of infinite capability
method.plain: Human life, as revealed by the Art, is a pure fire capable of education and improvement beyond other creatures.
method.voice: QUOTED: the more modern class of adepts

method.veiled: the object was not simply to obtain the Matter or prove it only, but to improve, perfect, and bring the Causal light to manifestation
method.plain: The aim is not merely to obtain or prove the matter but to perfect it and make the Causal light manifest; reasons for choosing 'the most noble subject' and 'this only vessel' are said to be given in this philosophy.

also.text: why the most noble subject was chosen, and this only vessel for its elaboration

method.veiled: in what our human circulatory system differs and occultly approximates, so that it can be made to comprehend all inferior existences, and supersede nature in her course
method.plain: The human circulatory system can be made to comprehend all lower existences and surpass nature's course; how is to be gathered from this philosophy, not explained here.

method.veiled: the medium is always in the circulation produced from the action and reaction of centrifugal and centripetal forces
method.plain: Circulation mediates between attraction and repulsion; when they are equal it forms a circle and harmonizes them, if the matter is suitably qualified; predominance of either gives an ellipse.

also.text: when they are in equilibrium, a circle is produced
will succeed if the matter be duly qualified for it

method.veiled: the wheel of human life turns forth, deviating from its axis, into a line which terminated finally in dissolution
method.plain: Since nature lost her original balance, human life runs off-center toward death.

also.text: nature has fallen off from her original balance

method.veiled: their Antimonial Spirit rectified by Art, being in bright lines of equal attraction and repulsion, as it were a perfect magnet in a star-like circle of irradiated circulation
method.plain: Only one Matter can be so harmonized; only the Antimonial Spirit, rectified by Art and with equal attraction and repulsion, can withstand life's drift to dissolution.

also.text: there is but One Matter truly qualifiable or capable of qualifying matter to be harmonized in this way

method.veiled: the agent in the preparation of this spirit, continues Bohme, is the Invisible Mercury
method.plain: The Invisible Universal Mercury (spiritual air of Antimony), held in a suitable vehicle, prepares the spirit; its action is to harmonize attraction, repulsion and circulation.

also.text: condensed in its proper vehicle in any of the degrees of permanency
the Principle of its operation consists in the power of harmonizing the three discordant principles

method.veiled: this is the vital spirit of the arterial blood, where the universal principles are in their natural generation unequally composed
method.plain: The vital spirit of the arterial blood is where the three principles are unequally composed: repulsion outweighs inner attraction, so life flows outward and consciousness is turned from its First Cause.
method.basis: II.1 ¶21; referent of 'this' uncertain (see ambiguities); voice after n17 unclear.

also.text: the total circulatory life is expulsive, and drawn without to a debilitated consciousness away from its First Cause

method.veiled: by occultation of the opposive principle, to restore the true rector to his original rule
method.plain: The Art suppresses the dominant opposing (repulsive) force so that the proper governing principle rules again, reversing the outward drift of life.
method.basis: II.1 ¶21: the disorder named just before is repulsion predominating over interior attraction; the remedy is of 'this inverse order'.

method.veiled: sanquinis salem per urinaceum fermentum sic transmutari debere, ut ultiman vitam amittat, mediamque servet, salsedinemque retineat
method.plain: (Our translation) The salt of blood is to be transmuted by a urinous ferment so it loses its last life, keeps its middle life and retains its saltiness. This chunk does not explain it.
method.basis: II.1 ¶21 Latin, translation ours only.

method.veiled: Sove, Coagula, Fige
method.plain: Dissolve the fixed, make it volatile, then fix the volatile. This chunk gives no further explanation.
method.basis: II.1 ¶22 Latin couplet, translation ours.

also.text: Si fixum solvas faciasque volare solutum Et volucrem figas

method.veiled: to mortify and induce generation, to vivify the spirit, to cleanse and introduce light, until they fight and contend with each other, and grow white and freed form their defilements, rising, as it were, from blackness and darkness
method.plain: Sequence: mortification, then generation, vivifying the spirit, cleansing and illumination, a struggle, and emergence from black to white.

method.veiled: in three months circulation, says he, by digestion, the powder becomes black, the opposition of attraction and repulsion ceases (in the vital spirit)
method.plain: After about three months of circulation by digestion, the matter turns black and still: the three principles stop opposing and rest.

also.text: sunk down black and motionless
the attraction of the fixed which produced the repulsion of the volatile, is slain by the circulation which also dies itself, and all three enter into rest

method.veiled: the head of Hermes’ crow is said to be in the beginning of this work
method.plain: 'Crow's head' names this black, motionless state at the beginning of the work.
method.basis: II.1 ¶23: 'And thus' links the name to the blackening just described; the identification is implied, not stated.

method.veiled: that which at first was fixed, viz., the sentient medium, is dissolved
method.plain: The fixed element dissolved in the blackening is the sentient medium; deeper working exposes the original evil in the matter and with it the principle of correction.
method.basis: II.1 ¶23 gives the gloss 'viz., the sentient medium'.

also.text: the original evil is made manifest in the matter to be renewed, and hence the principle of amendment and rectification also will appear, and on either side it is a signal of Art

ambiguities.quote: And these three principles of attraction, repulsion, and circulation, the universal accord of life, are everywhere and in all.
readings: Identifies salt, mercury and sulfur with attraction, repulsion and circulation.
Introduces the three forces as a parallel triad without asserting identity.
ambiguities.basis: Reading 1: 'these three principles' directly follows 'salt, mercury, and sulfur'. Reading 2: no explicit 'is' or 'that is'; the triad is then developed independently in ¶18-19.

ambiguities.quote: and this is the vital spirit of the arterial blood
readings: 'this' = the Invisible Mercury / spirit just discussed.
'this' = the Principle of harmonizing the three principles.
'this' = the field where the three principles act, i.e. the material on which the Art works.
ambiguities.basis: ¶21: the clause follows both 'the Invisible Universal Mercury' and 'the Principle of its operation'; what follows describes the blood's disorder as what the Art remedies.

ambiguities.quote: to restore the true rector to his original rule
readings: The interior attraction, over which repulsion now predominates.
The First Cause, from which consciousness has been drawn away.
ambiguities.basis: ¶21 names both: 'repulsive force so far predominating over the interior attraction' and 'away from its First Cause'.

ambiguities.quote: See out the noblest, as I said before
readings: The noblest = the noblest blood or part within a body.
ambiguities.basis: ¶12 'man, ys most noble creature'; ¶17 'the most noble subject'. The verse itself does not name the noblest.

ambiguities.quote: Attraction is the first principle of motion in nature
readings: ¶18-20 are Bohme's words, since ¶21 says 'continues Bohme'.
¶18-19 are Atwood's own exposition, with Bohme taken up only from ¶20 (n16).
ambiguities.basis: ¶21 'continues Bohme' implies a prior Bohme passage; n16 is attached at the end of ¶20; ¶18-19 carry no attribution.

translations.translation: Not translated in the book; stands in apposition to 'the true fiery water'. 'mayim' appears to mean 'water'; full rendering uncertain.

translations.original: Omne Aurum est aes, sed non omne aes est aurum
translations.translation: All gold is bronze (aes), but not all bronze is gold.

translations.original: Sanquinem urinamque pariter dat nobis natura, et ab horum natura salem dat Pyrotechnia, quem circulat ares in salem Paracelsi. Hoc addam: sanquinis salem per urinaceum fermentum sic transmutari debere, ut ultiman vitam amittat, mediamque servet, salsedinemque retineat
translations.translation: Nature gives us blood and urine alike, and from their nature Pyrotechnia (the fire-art) gives a salt, which 'ares' circulates into the salt of Paracelsus. This I will add: the salt of blood must be so transmuted by a urinous ferment that it loses its last life, keeps its middle one, and retains its saltiness. ('ares' unclear as printed.)

translations.original: Si fixum solvas faciasque volare solutum Et volucrem figas, faciunt tutum Sove, Coagula, Fige.
translations.translation: If you dissolve the fixed and make the dissolved fly, and fix the winged, they make [you] safe. Dissolve, Coagulate, Fix. ('Sove' read as 'Solve'.)

threads.note: 'Such are the distinctive assertions of one esteemed an adept' points back to the adept quoted in the preceding chunk.
'The foregoing evidence ... may help to lead on the inquiry to a more explicit ground' points forward; the ground is not specified.
'may reasons are given why the most noble subject was chosen, and this only vessel' refers to reasons given in 'this philosophy', not supplied here.
'as was before observed' points to the earlier statement (¶19 itself) that equilibrium forms a circle.
'our modern exponent' refers to a modern source cited earlier, apparently the one of ¶18-21 (Bohme per ¶21); not named in ¶23.
